field.embedded_credentials: The address must not contain a user name or password
field.scheme: Only http and https are supported
field.not_absolute: Enter an absolute path inside the container
field.not_empty: The target directory is not empty. Choose a new one
field.not_mounted: This directory is not on a mounted volume; restored data would vanish with the container

field.inside_data: Cannot restore into tern's own data directory

shell.zone: Times are in the node time zone, {{zone}}

keyfile.title_mismatch: The key file does not match
keyfile.body_missing: tern cannot find the key file that opens its credential vault, so the vault stays closed and no scheduled task runs.
keyfile.body_mismatch: The key file in the secrets directory is not the one this vault was created with, so the vault stays closed and no scheduled task runs.
keyfile.fix: Mount the original secrets directory back into the container, then restart the container.
keyfile.note: There is nothing to do on this page: it can only be fixed on the host.

v.node_name: Only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit

setup.title: Set up tern
setup.password_hint: At least 10 characters. Used to log in here.
setup.node_name_hint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. nas-home
setup.mode_keyfile_desc: Unlocks by itself after a restart, so scheduled tasks keep running. Keep the secrets directory apart from data.
setup.mode_passphrase_desc: Safer, but after every restart someone must enter the passphrase here; until then no scheduled task runs.
setup.summary_note: The admin password and passphrase are not shown here; make sure you keep them.

login.title: Log in
login.wait: Too many attempts. Try again in {{n}} s

unlock.title: Unlock the vault
unlock.desc: tern has restarted and needs the passphrase to open its stored credentials. No scheduled task runs until then.

conn.title: Connections & keys
conn.no_keys: No keys yet. Generate or import one on the Keys tab first.
conn.probe_hint: Before saving, fetch the remote's host fingerprint and check it on the remote.
conn.probe_check: On the remote, run ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_{{alg}}_key.pub; it should print the same.
conn.confirm_fingerprint: I have checked this fingerprint on the remote
conn.password_keep: Saved; leave empty to keep it
conn.in_use: Tasks still use this connection: {{names}}. Delete or change them first.

test_result.network: Cannot reach the remote. Check the address and whether the network between them is up
test_result.auth: The remote refused authentication. Check that the public key is on the remote, or the WebDAV user name and password
test_result.host_key: The remote's fingerprint has changed. If you did not reinstall the remote, someone may be impersonating it. Once you are sure, edit this connection to fetch and confirm the fingerprint again

keys.empty: No SSH keys yet. Generate one, or import an existing private key.
keys.generate_desc: Generates an ed25519 key. The private key stays in tern's vault and is never shown anywhere.
keys.private_key_hint: Paste an ed25519, ecdsa or rsa private key in PEM form. It is never shown again.
keys.add_to_authorized: Add this line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the remote
keys.delete_confirm: Delete the key "{{name}}"? Remove its line from authorized_keys on the remote yourself.
keys.in_use: Connections still use this key. Delete or change those connections first, then delete the key.

task.title: Tasks
task.type_backup_desc: Back up local directories with restic to a repository over SSH, keeping many versions.
task.type_sync_desc: One-way sync of folder pairs to a remote, or back from it.
task.name: Name
task.enabled_hint: When disabled the schedule does not fire; you can still run it by hand.
task.cron_hint: 5 fields: minute hour day month weekday, in the node time zone.
task.catch_up_hint: If tern was down at a scheduled time, run once after it starts.
task.stale_auto: Empty means automatic: {{d}} (twice the schedule period)
task.stale_auto_plain: Empty means automatic (twice the schedule period)
task.max_runtime_hint: Empty means unlimited. Over time the run is stopped and marked failed; retry waits count.
task.delays: Wait before each retry (minutes, comma separated)
task.hook_script_hint: Leave empty to run nothing. Runs with sh.
task.hook_ssh: The remote of an SSH connection
task.hook_warning: Anyone who can log in here can run any command in the container through this.
task.excludes_hint: Two forms: a name rule without a slash such as *.tmp, or an anchored rule starting with a slash such as /cache/.
task.repo_path_hint: A directory on the remote. Empty or missing: a new repository is created; an existing one is opened with the password below.
task.repo_password_hint: Before saving you get the recovery information; the task is created only after you confirm you kept it.
task.protocol_hint: Many large files or a poor network: prefer rsync.
task.mirror_warning: Files that exist only at the destination are deleted.
task.max_deletes_hint: Above this the run stops; allow it once from the run's page.
task.conflict: This task was changed somewhere else.
task.conflict_hint: Your changes are still in the form. Reloading replaces them with the latest version.
task.not_found: This task does not exist; it may have been deleted.
task.delete_confirm: Delete the task "{{name}}" and its run history? Data on the remote is not touched.
task.recovery_desc: If this machine dies, the repository password dies with it and the backups can never be opened. Keep the information below somewhere other than this machine.
task.recovery_confirm: I have kept the recovery information somewhere other than this machine
task.cmd_desc: Running these by hand does the same thing. Credentials are not included; supply them yourself.
task.repo_password_source: Where the repository password comes from

overview.title: Overview
overview.stale: {{count}} tasks have gone too long without a success
overview.empty: No tasks yet. Add a connection under Connections & keys, then create a task under Tasks.

bbr.title: BBR
bbr.supported: The kernel supports BBR, but the current algorithm is {{current}}. Add the line below under sysctls in the compose file, then recreate the container
bbr.missing: The host kernel has not loaded the tcp_bbr module. Run the command below on the host, then recreate the container
bbr.note: BBR only helps data this node sends, that is pushes and backups. For pulls it is up to the remote.

run.title: Runs
run.not_found: This run does not exist; it may have been cleaned up.
run.allow_body: tern stopped this sync to protect your data, for the reason below. Confirming reruns it once without the deletion limit; later runs are limited as before.

snap.title: Snapshots & restore
snap.loading: Reading the repository; on a slow network this can take a while…
snap.empty: The repository has no snapshots yet.
snap.restore_desc: Restores into a new or empty directory, never over the original. The directory must be on a mounted volume.
snap.subpath_hint: Restore only this directory or file of the snapshot, e.g. /data/docs/2024.

rec.title: Recovery information
rec.desc: The repository password is shown here only; closing clears it. Enter the admin password first.

settings.title: Settings
settings.node_name_hint: For display. The restic --host a backup task recorded at creation does not change.
settings.timezone_hint: Set by the container's TZ environment variable.
settings.timezone_unknown: TZ is not set in the container, so times here are shown in UTC.
